content:
STAGE: read scope contract + all 9 proposals + shared evidence bundle
GOAL: fix the reading of the rubric anchors and the shared ledger before scoring anything.
READ: the nine idea specs (behaviour_anchored_geodesic_charts, BRANCHCURV-SID, SUCC-TAN-RQ, GEOPFX-SID, GEO-SHELL-RQ, GYRO-TARGET-RQ, KAPPA_BRANCH, GEO_REPAIR, LORENTZ_CONE_RQ) and the per-proposal evidence bundles.
OBSERVED: every bundle carries the same measured blocks E5 (successor-entropy stratification, top1 mass 0.4375 -> 0.0543, Spearman -0.973, bin item counts), E6 (width-20 beam survival / recall@10 for already-measured arms: l1_br 0.04671, l1_br_euclid 0.06207, l1_only 0.06233, resample 0.06363, successor_entropy 0.05122, successor_geodesic_coarse 0.05500, successor_geodesic_coarse_v2 0.05463, tangent_successor_residual 0.05500), E7 (teacher-forced NLL; l1_br T1..T4 = 0/0/0/9.03), E8 (first-level capacity ceiling: 0.3106 at K=16 down to 0.0822 at K=256), E11 (same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067), E10 (edges 118315, mean out-degree 5.45).
REASONING: E6 is the ledger: a hyperbolic/tangent successor mechanism (successor_geodesic_coarse, tangent_successor_residual) has already been trained and came in at 0.055, well under the 0.065 target. Any proposal in that family must be scored low on novelty/exploration, and E11 (9.07% prefix agreement vs 6.7% permuted) caps how strongly any prefix-behaviour claim can be supported.
OPEN: whether the geometric necessity of each candidate survives a matched Euclidean reduction; checked per proposal next.
WHERE: n/a (no bundle file read outside the prompt).

STAGE: geometric reduction checks (the decisive pass)
GOAL: for each candidate, decide whether the curved primitive is doing work a matched Euclidean control cannot reproduce, and look for algebraic/domain failures.
READ: the SPECIFICATION/GEOMETRIC_NECESSITY equations of the nine proposals.
OBSERVED:
 (a) SUCC-TAN-RQ: curvature is fixed at k0 = -1/median||z||^2, so log_0 and exp_0 are a FIXED radial diffeomorphism R; s_i = R^{-1}(R(u_i)+eta*t_i). Curvature factors out; behaviour is entirely in the Euclidean tangent mean t_i. Geometry necessity capped at 2.
 (b) BRANCHCURV-SID: u_i = exp_0^{k0}(z_i) lives in the ball of radius 1/sqrt(|k0|) but is scored with d_{kappa_k}, kappa_k up to 4*k0, i.e. radius halved. For ||u_i||^2 = 0.9/|k0| and kappa_k = 4|k0| the factor (1-kappa_k||u_i||^2) = -2.6 -> arcosh argument below 1 -> NaN. Genuine domain/scale mismatch.
 (c) LORENTZ_CONE_RQ: on one hyperboloid sheet <y-x,y-x>_L = <y,y>-2<x,y>+<x,x> = -2/c^2-2(-(1/c^2)cosh(c d)) = (2/c^2)(cosh(c d)-1) >= 0 for every pair. The "future cone" condition <=0 holds only at d=0, so the cone-violation observable is identically 0 and the hinge is an always-active transition-mass-weighted squared geodesic distance, i.e. an ATTRACTION between the pairs, not a causal order. Numeric check c=1, d=1: 2(cosh1-1)=1.086>0.
 (d) KAPPA_BRANCH: h_i = H_i/log(|S_i|+1) evaluated on E5 bins gives 0.931/1.335=0.70, 1.505/1.723=0.87, 1.875/2.041=0.92, 2.362/2.485=0.95, 3.405/3.813=0.89 -> kappa_i in about [1.70,1.95] on a kappa0=1 scale, a ~15% field. Mechanically sound (kbar <= max(kappa_i,kappa_j) so the ball argument stays >0), but the field is nearly constant.
 (e) GYRO-TARGET-RQ: eta_i = c_i/(1+c_i) <= 1/2, b_i = exp_{p_i}(eta_i * mean log_{p_i}(p_j)); two items with identical successor sets and c_i get the identical b_i and therefore the identical nearest code.
 (f) GEO_REPAIR: the Poincare rank of candidate codes from a Frechet mean is a post-hoc decision rule with no gradient; a Euclidean nearest-code rule is a close surrogate.
REASONING: (a)-(f) fix the geometry_necessity numbers: only the per-item gauge and per-code/per-item curvature candidates plausibly exceed Euclidean (3); the rest are 2.
OPEN: none, the reductions are explicit.
WHERE: prompt bundles E12-E16 per proposal.

STAGE: FINAL ANSWER (complete scoring, printed in full in the response)
GOAL: hand in scores, scope verdicts, evidence, objections, counterexamples, rationales for all nine proposals.
OBSERVED (the decisive checks):
- BRANCHCURV: u_i lives in the k0 ball (radius 1/sqrt|k0|) but is scored with d_{kappa_k}, kappa_k up to 4k0; at ||u_i||^2=0.9/|k0| the factor 1-4*0.9=-2.6 -> arcosh argument <1, NaN.
- LORENTZ_CONE: <y-x,y-x>_L = (2/c^2)(cosh(cd)-1) >= 0 identically on one sheet, so the future-cone condition <=0 holds only at d=0; the hinge is an always-active mass-weighted geodesic ATTRACTION and the "cone violation rate" observable is identically 1, not movable (c=1,d=1 gives 1.086).
- SUCC-TAN: fixed k0 => log_0/exp_0 is a fixed radial diffeo R, s_i = R^-1(R(u_i)+eta t_i); curvature factors out.
- KAPPA_BRANCH: h_i = H_i/log(|S_i|+1) on E5 bins = 0.70/0.87/0.92/0.95/0.89 -> kappa in ~[1.70,1.95], a near-constant field.
- GEO-SHELL: radius rho is an increasing function of B_g by definition, so the "broad communities get bigger radius" observable is a tautology; delta is an underived constant.
- GEO_REPAIR: repair is post-optimiser on assignment only, no gradient; identical successor sets get identical centroids so the collision survives repair.
- GYRO-TARGET / behaviour_anchored feed the dominant moves onto successor barycentres / per-item anchors (collapse risk, ||a_i|| degeneracy UNKNOWN).
SCORES: behaviour_anchored 3/3/2/4/4/4/2 IN_SCOPE; BRANCHCURV 4/3/3/4/3/3/3 IN_SCOPE; SUCC-TAN 3/2/1/4/3/3/1 IN_SCOPE; GEOPFX 3/3/3/3/3/3/3 IN_SCOPE; GEO-SHELL 3/2/2/2/3/3/3 IN_SCOPE; GYRO-TARGET 4/3/3/4/4/4/3 IN_SCOPE; KAPPA_BRANCH 4/3/3/4/4/4/3 IN_SCOPE; GEO_REPAIR 3/2/3/4/4/3/3 IN_SCOPE; LORENTZ_CONE 3/2/3/2/3/3/3 IN_SCOPE.
REASONING: no arm run, no Recall predicted, no ranking between proposals; E6 is treated as the ledger (successor_geodesic_coarse 0.05500, tangent_successor_residual 0.05500) which caps novelty/exploration for the SUCC-TAN and anchored-chart family.
OPEN: two UNKNOWNs, each with its bounded check: ||a_i||/s histogram for behaviour_anchored; the frozen-baseline SID group-size histogram for GEO_REPAIR.

SCORE: behaviour_anchored_geodesic_charts | behavior_evidence=4 | geometry_necessity=3 | novelty=3 | downstream_mechanism=4 | falsifiability=4 | implementability=4 | exploration_value=4
SCOPE: behaviour_anchored_geodesic_charts | IN_SCOPE | behaviour (top-8 successor Frechet-mean anchor a_i) and curvature (log_{a_i} / geodesic exp residual chain) meet inside the one primitive that emits every code, so setting a_i = 0 changes every SID; the hypothesis does name the behaviour-off and geometry-off configurations. Missing: the matched Euclidean control is only named, not specified (the natural one is anchor at the Euclidean neighbour mean with q_l compared to r_l by L2), so the geometry-off arm has to be defined by the implementer.
EVIDENCE: behaviour_anchored_geodesic_charts | E1 E2 E3 E4 E5 E6 E8 E10 E11 E12 E13
OBJECTION: the anchor safeguard is dimensionally inconsistent and the codebook comparison is frame-dependent: "clamped to radius 0.5 s" compares a Poincare-ball radius (max 1) with s = median ||z_i||, a tangent-space norm, and q_l in C_l is compared with r_1 = log_{a_i}(p_i) in T_{a_i} while the next code is applied at a different base, with no parallel transport or common frame between anchors, so "the same tuple means the same displacement from my own anchor" is not a well-defined invariant statement.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: with s >= 2 (a plausible median Stage-1 norm in 64 dimensions) 0.5 s >= 1 exceeds the ball radius, so the clamp never acts and is not a safeguard at all; with s = 0.4 every anchor is confined to a disc of ball radius 0.2, whose hyperbolic volume is ~0.2^d of the ball, so all anchors essentially coincide with the origin and the both-on mechanism is numerically the geometry-off arm.
RATIONALE: behaviour_evidence=4 because the premise that a single flat content code system wastes prefix capacity is measured, not assumed: E8 gives the K-capacity curve (0.3106 shared-cluster share at K=16 falling to 0.0822 at K=256) and E5 shows the successor-entropy spread (top-1 mass 0.4375 vs 0.0543) with 4895 items per bin; it is not 5 because the direct prefix statistic E11 is weak (0.0907 vs 0.067 permuted null), so the specific "successors should share prefixes" reading is partially supported. geometry_necessity=3: the anchored chart is a real curved operation (E12/E13) plausibly beyond Euclidean, but the obvious Euclidean competitor (subtract the neighbourhood centroid, then residual-quantise) reproduces the displacement-from-anchor idea, and the missing frame identification plus the vacuous clamp leave a cancellation channel open, so 4 is not defensible. novelty=3: it is a distinct coupling position from the ledger entries successor_geodesic_coarse (0.05500), successor_entropy (0.05122) and tangent_successor_residual (0.05500), because behaviour sets the gauge rather than the shift or a loss; it is not argued against our ledger item by item. downstream_mechanism=4: the assignment change (level-1 agreement over transition pairs) and the expected effect are named. falsifiability=4: both switches plus diagnostics (code-agreement rate, mean shared prefix, Jaccard, recall) and the 0.065 criterion are stated. implementability=4: differentiable (detached anchors, straight-through commitment), guarded, cost plausibly ~1.05x but unaudited. exploration_value=4. Uncertainty: E4 is the only data-contract item I have and the encoder-collapse risk is untested; the bounded check is to print the ||p_i|| distribution at epoch 0 (if the median norm is below ~0.1 the anchors are noise) and the cross-anchor frame test is to check whether codes are stable under a global rotation of z.

SCORE: BRANCHCURV-SID | behavior_evidence=4 | geometry_necessity=2 | novelty=2 | downstream_mechanism=4 | falsifiability=3 | implementability=3 | exploration_value=3
SCOPE: BRANCHCURV-SID | IN_SCOPE | the successor-branching entropy H_k sets the per-code curvature kappa_k that enters the nearest-code distance and the soft assignment, so behaviour changes the metric and the metric changes the emitted SID; removing H_k (H_k = Hbar) sets kappa_k = k0 and removing the curve sets a Euclidean distance. Missing: the three comparisons are not written out as switches in the text (only "no ablation arm trained" is stated), so the switch wiring is inferable but not specified.
EVIDENCE: BRANCHCURV-SID | E1 E2 E3 E5 E6 E8 E10 E12 E13 E14
OBJECTION: the per-code curvature acts only at second order in the ball radius, because the sqrt(kappa) prefactor cancels against the arcosh argument, and the per-code field additionally destroys the metric property of d, so nearest-code cells can overlap and the assignment can oscillate; the clamp and the post-500 freeze change the schedule, not the non-metricity.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: for the stated distance, d_k(u,v) = (1/sqrt k) arcosh(1 + 2k||u-v||^2/((1-k||u||^2)(1-k||v||^2))) = 2||u-v|| * (1 + O(k(||u||^2+||v||^2))) as k||.||^2 -> 0; with ||u|| = 0.2 and kappa doubled, d^2 moves by about 7 percent, so two candidate codes whose Euclidean distances differ by more than 7 percent are ranked identically with and without the whole curvature field, and a per-code multiplicative bias b_k on the squared Euclidean distance reproduces the leading term exactly.
RATIONALE: behaviour_evidence=4: E5 measures the branching heterogeneity that the mechanism keys on (bins from H=0.931, support 2.8, top1 0.438 to H=3.405, support 44.3, top1 0.054, Spearman -0.973), and E10 gives the graph coverage (118315 edges, mean out-degree 5.45); it is not 5 because the causal claim "one global curvature is the bottleneck" is not itself measured. geometry_necessity=2 because the curvature's leading-order cancellation means a matched Euclidean transform (per-code bias/temperature) reproduces most of the ranking; the argument that behaviour must change the metric is asserted, not argued against that control. novelty=2: this is a routine variation of the measured successor_entropy arm (E6: 0.05122, below the best ledger arm 0.06363); a sibling proposal in this same round, KAPPA_BRANCH, is the same computation with a per-item rather than per-code field, which I note without ranking. downstream_mechanism=4: the assignment change (per-code occupancy and successor entropy of the top-1 next token) and the expected direction are named. falsifiability=3: the safe-failure statement plus the diagnostic exist, but the three matched controls are not written into the mechanism. implementability=3: differentiable but the arcosh argument needs an explicit clamp (argument >= 1) that is not stated, and the per-code curvature histogram/schedule is extra state. exploration_value=3. Uncertainty: the size of the curvature effect depends on where the encoder puts the points, which the bundle does not report; bounded check: measure the median ball radius of u_i at epoch 0 and, if it is below ~0.3, the field is provably near-inert.

SCORE: SUCC-TAN-RQ | behavior_evidence=3 | geometry_necessity=2 | novelty=1 | downstream_mechanism=3 | falsifiability=2 | implementability=3 | exploration_value=0
SCOPE: SUCC-TAN-RQ | IN_SCOPE | the successor tangent t_i is transported by exp_0 and enters the level-1 base point of the residual chain, so behaviour is inside the quantiser primitive. Missing: none of the three switches is named, and the CHANGE text ("the chain reconstructs s_i") contradicts the specification's two-term loss.
EVIDENCE: SUCC-TAN-RQ | E1 E2 E3 E5 E6 E7 E10 E12 E13 E14
OBJECTION: shifting the current item toward its mean successor erases the current/next distinction the generator needs, and "the code chain is chosen to reconstruct s_i" is false for the stated loss, which also contains d(u_i, u_hat) with equal weight, so the chain reconstructs a compromise point between i and its successor mean.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: for a deterministic pair (c_ij = 1, |S_i| = 1) t_i = log_0(u_j) - log_0(u_i) and eta = d_code/||t_i||, so s_i lies exactly one code spacing from u_i toward u_j; if the pair separation is itself about d_code then s_i lands on u_j's point and c_1(s_i) is u_j's level-1 cell, so i and j share the full SID with high probability and become indistinguishable.
RATIONALE: behavior_evidence=3 (E5 successor mass is measured, but "residual bits are spent arbitrarily" is not); geometry_necessity=2 (a Euclidean shift plus Euclidean residual code is a matched control that reproduces the construction to first order); novelty=1 because the ledger already contains tangent_successor_residual at 0.05500 with depth-4 prefix survival 0.073 - if that arm is this computation the score is 0, and the bounded check is to read that ledger implementation; downstream_mechanism=3; falsifiability=2 (no controls stated); implementability=3 (no boundary clip on xi_l named); exploration_value=0 (repeats a measured negative in the same family).

FINAL (compact; full blocks in the reply). nine scores:
behaviour_anchored_geodesic_charts IN_SCOPE 4/3/3/4/4/4/4 (E1-E6,E8,E10-E13; objection: 0.5s clamp mixes tangent norm with ball radius, no cross-anchor frame)
BRANCHCURV-SID IN_SCOPE 4/2/2/4/3/3/3 (kappa cancels to leading order: d_k=2||u-v||(1+O(k r^2)); per-code bias reproduces)
SUCC-TAN-RQ IN_SCOPE 3/2/1/3/2/3/0 (near-repeat of ledger tangent_successor_residual 0.05500; shift erases current/next distinction)
GEOPFX-SID IN_SCOPE(marginal) 3/3/2/3/2/3/1 (L_geo identically 0 when LCP=0; 91% of pairs, per E11 0.0907)
GEO-SHELL-RQ IN_SCOPE 4/3/3/3/3/2/3 (Sarkar r=(N-B)/(N+B) puts hubs at the centre, contradicting its hypothesis; delta undefined)
GYRO-TARGET-RQ IN_SCOPE 3/2/3/2/4/4/4 (identical successor sets give identical target, merged items undecodable)
KAPPA_BRANCH IN_SCOPE 4/2/2/4/3/3/3 (h_i near 0 for low degree, field near constant; not a metric)
GEO_REPAIR OUT_OF_SCOPE 2/2/3/3/2/3/3 (no real coupling: post-hoc suffix on unchanged quantiser; collision premise unmeasured; no-op if SIDs distinct)
LORENTZ_CONE_RQ IN_SCOPE 3/1/3/3/3/2/2 (future cone empty on hyperboloid: <y-x,y-x>_L=2(cosh(t-u)-1)/c^2>=0, equality iff x=y)
Caveat: E6 internal payload reports l1_br recall 0.04068 vs 0.04671 summary (abs diff 0.006), larger than the 0.0014 gap from best ledger arm 0.06363 to 0.065.
